verifiable.explanation: The verifier runs the agent's intake.py on 30 hidden certificates against a fixed, pre-generated truth set via deterministic JSON comparison (compare.py, with Unicode NFKC/casefold/whitespace-stripping normalization per policy rule 4). No LLM-as-judge, no live services, no network installs at verify time (all deps baked into tests/Dockerfile). Grading is a pure programmatic diff against ground truth.

solvable.explanation: solution/intake.py (1225 lines) is a complete, working implementation covering every policy rule (OCR-first reading, text-layer reconciliation, revision handling, unit conversion/rounding, limit matching, disposition). The README states it passes all 30 hidden certificates and 185/185 across five generator seeds, well within the 120s/cert limit. The approach (render pages, OCR, reconcile with text layer, parse tables/revisions, apply decimal arithmetic) is a coherent, implementable strategy for an expert familiar with PDF/OCR tooling.

difficult.explanation: The task requires building a robust OCR+parsing pipeline that handles rotated scans, missing/misleading text layers, stamped corrections, multi-page revisions, unit conversion with rounding semantics, and multi-rule disposition logic across four distinct supplier document styles. This is well beyond an average undergraduate exercise and requires genuine document-engineering and careful rule-following expertise.

interesting.explanation: Certificate-of-analysis intake against a house specification is a real quality-control workflow at supplement/pharma manufacturers, as described by the author's own professional background. Building reliable automated intake tooling for messy supplier PDFs is a genuine real-world problem with commercial value.

outcome_verified.explanation: Grading is purely on intake.py's output JSON compared field-by-field to expected values; no particular library, OCR engine, or coding approach is mandated. The agent is free to implement reading/parsing however it likes as long as the final JSON matches policy semantics.

anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: Hidden certificates, their specs, and truth JSON live only in tests/ (verifier image), never shipped to the agent image. The agent only sees 7 sample certificates in environment/samples/. The separate-verifier mode tears down the agent container before verification, and /tests and /logs/verifier are chmod 700 before the agent's tool runs under nobody, so the tool cannot read truth or write the reward.

task_security.explanation: All Dockerfiles, scripts, and solution code perform only legitimate PDF/OCR setup, test execution, and comparison logic. No credential exfiltration, no obfuscated code, no network calls beyond pinned package installs at build time, no host-escape attempts.

functional_verification.explanation: The verifier executes the submitted intake.py as a subprocess on real PDF inputs and compares its JSON output field-by-field against ground truth (compare.py) — this is genuine output/behavior checking, not string/keyword scanning of source code.

deterministic_reproducible.explanation: All pip packages are version-pinned identically in both Dockerfiles; apt packages are unpinned per convention. Tesseract OCR and the parsing logic are deterministic given fixed input PDFs; no live external services are used. Given the reference solution's claimed 185/185 pass rate across generator seeds, the verifier should reproduce consistently.

essential_difficulty.explanation: Failures stem from genuine reading/parsing/reasoning challenges (OCR on unusual fonts, stamp detection, revision resolution, unit conversion), not from arbitrary output formatting — the output schema (policy rule 9) is simple and explicit, and string comparison is whitespace/case-insensitive, minimizing clerical failure modes.

test_instruction_alignment.explanation: instruction.md points to policy.md as the normative spec; every output field and disposition rule tested in compare.py/test_outputs.py traces directly to policy.md rules 3-9. No extraneous requirements are introduced in tests, and all policy requirements (identity fields, result rows, disposition) are covered by the comparison logic.

novel.explanation: This is a custom synthetic-document-generation task with bespoke supplier styles, policy rules, and edge cases (stamps, revisions, continuation pages, OCR misreads) that cannot be solved by recalling a known textbook algorithm or memorized solution.

agentic.explanation: Solving this requires iterative exploration of sample PDFs/specs, writing and debugging an OCR pipeline, testing against samples, and refining parsing logic across many edge cases — this cannot be done in a single zero-shot generation and requires sustained environment interaction.

reviewable.explanation: Expected outputs are derived from a generator (per README) rather than hardcoded, and sample certificates with expected.json let a reviewer inspect the PDF, spec, and expected output side by side to sanity-check rule application without deep OCR expertise.

instruction_concision.explanation: instruction.md is a short, human-written paragraph using absolute paths (/app/intake/intake.py, /app/policy.md, /app/samples/) and describes what to achieve (read certificates, apply policy, write JSON) without prescribing how to implement the OCR/parsing pipeline.

effective_instruction_length.explanation: instruction.md itself is very short (~4 sentences); the referenced policy.md (9 concise numbered rules, ~700 words) is necessary normative content that defines the exact semantics the output must satisfy. No unnecessary repetition or fragmentation is present in either document.

solution_quality.explanation: solution/intake.py is a genuine, non-trivial computation (OCR, parsing, decimal-based comparisons) kept as its own file rather than inlined in solve.sh; solve.sh simply installs it, which is appropriate since the deliverable itself is the solution artifact, not a precomputed answer.

separate_verifier_configured.explanation: artifacts = ["/app/intake/"] is the only input needed by the verifier; tests/Dockerfile bakes all verifier tooling (tesseract, poppler, pinned pip packages, pytest, setpriv/pkill) with no runtime installs in test.sh. Shared pinned package versions between environment/Dockerfile and tests/Dockerfile match exactly, so no drift exists.

environment_hygiene.explanation: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs policy.md and samples/ (agent-facing resources), never tests/ or solution/; it does not include pytest or other test-only deps. tests/Dockerfile owns /tests/*, pre-installs pytest/pytest-json-ctrf and util-linux/procps for isolation. Apt installs in both Dockerfiles are unpinned with apt-get update preceding and rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* cleanup following.

structured_data_schema.explanation: policy.md rule 9 explicitly enumerates the exact output JSON schema (top-level {"lots": [...]}, exact per-lot keys, exact per-result-row keys), making the expected structure normative rather than example-only.

typos.explanation: No typos were found in file paths, command invocations (python3 /app/intake/intake.py IN.pdf SPEC.json OUT.json), variable names, or Dockerfile instructions across the reviewed files.

difficulty_explanation_quality.explanation: README's Difficulty explanation concretely describes both reading challenges (misleading text layers, stamps, scrambled text, font variety) and policy-application challenges (revisions, unit conversion, LOQ handling) for a non-expert reader, notes the data is synthetic but modeled on real cases, and identifies the real-world role (QC desk / contract manufacturer) that would perform this work.

solution_explanation_quality.explanation: README's Solution explanation accurately summarizes the actual approach in solution/intake.py (render-then-OCR reading reconciled with text layer, line-based parsing with revision resolution, decimal disposition logic), consistent with the code reviewed, and reports concrete verification numbers (185/185 across seeds, 18s worst case) supporting feasibility.

verification_explanation_quality.explanation: README's Verification explanation accurately describes the isolation setup (nobody execution, 700-permission /tests and /logs/verifier, pkill cleanup), the per-certificate pass criteria, and the NFKC/casefold/whitespace-insensitive string comparison, all matching test.sh/compare.py exactly. No inequality-based tolerances are used that would require separate calibration justification.

category_and_tags.explanation: category "Operations" / subcategory "Quality" fits a quality-control intake/disposition workflow rather than being a generic software task. Tags (pdf, ocr, document-extraction, quality-control, certificate-of-analysis, dietary-supplements) are specific and directly descriptive of the task's skills and domain.

task_name.explanation: The task identifier "coa-intake" (from task.toml's task.name) is concise, descriptive, kebab-case, and within the 3-word limit, clearly conveying the certificate-of-analysis intake theme.

resource_configuration.explanation: Verifier timeout (3600s) comfortably covers 30 certificates at up to 120s each plus pytest overhead; agent timeout (28800s/8h) is generous for a genuinely hard, multi-day-caliber engineering task; environment resources (2 CPU, 4GB RAM, 10GB storage) are modest and appropriate for OCR/PDF processing rather than being inflated for artificial difficulty.

task_readme.explanation: README.md contains all required sections (Task Metadata, Difficulty explanation, Solution explanation, Verification explanation, Relevant experience) with accurate, non-redundant content beyond the instruction/solution files themselves.

expert_time_estimate.explanation: expert_time_estimate_hours = 6.0 is non-zero and plausible for a domain expert with prior experience building exactly this kind of OCR/intake pipeline (as the author claims to have), consistent with the agent timeout of 8 hours being somewhat larger to allow for exploration/debugging.

task_toml_schema.explanation: task.toml uses only recognized fields: [task] name/description/authors, [metadata] with standard fields, [verifier]/[verifier.environment], [agent], [environment], and root-level artifacts — no invented fields were found.

no_extraneous_files.explanation: Every file traces to a purpose: Dockerfiles reference policy.md/samples (environment) and tests content (tests/Dockerfile); solve.sh installs solution/intake.py; tests/hidden and tests/truth are consumed by test_outputs.py/compare.py. No stray editor/OS cruft or duplicate files were found.

artifact_efficiency.explanation: The sole artifact is /app/intake/ containing a single small Python file (the agent's actual deliverable) — minimal footprint with nothing build-time-fixed or redundant being shipped as an artifact.

verifier_execution_isolation.explanation: test.sh chmods /logs/verifier and /tests to 700 before any agent code runs, executes the submitted intake.py via setpriv as nobody with a timeout and output redirected to files (not pipes), kills leftover nobody processes after each run, and only root-run pytest (importing only trusted compare.py, never agent code) decides the reward from exit codes written during the unprivileged runs.

ctrf_reporting.explanation: test.sh invokes pytest with --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json against test_outputs.py, producing per-certificate CTRF results alongside the binary reward.

do_not_modify_enforced.explanation: instruction.md contains no do-not-modify/preserve constraint on any concrete artifact; the agent is simply asked to build a new tool at /app/intake/intake.py.

binary_reward.explanation: test.sh writes reward.txt as exactly 1 (pytest exit 0 = all certificates passed) or 0 (pytest exit 1 = some failed); any other pytest exit code is treated as a hard verifier error (exit 1, no reward written) rather than a fractional score. No continuous scoring path exists.
